summary: Open a project on another connected SSH machine: the target clones the repository from the remote the current branch tracks (a fork, not the repository it was forked from), checks out the same branch in a folder the user picks (default ~/projects/<name>; an existing folder must be empty), and lists the project at once. A clone in progress is recorded in a journal in the target's data folder, so after a backend restart the half-done folder is removed (only when its device and inode still match the folder the clone made) and status reads failed, and the dialog offers Try again. The desktop polls the clone, then copies only the ignored files the user picked (none by default; text, 1 MB each, no links, no install or build folders), reading each from the source backend and writing it to the target. A chat start in that project waits for the clone, and cached 'no favicon' and 'not a git repository' answers for the path are dropped when it ends.

reactNativeIos.reason: The phone app connects to one backend at a time and has no SSH machine list, so it cannot name a second machine to clone onto. The new project-clone channels need the terminal scope, which a paired phone never holds, so the phone cannot call them either. A project cloned from the desktop is an ordinary project row on the target and appears in the phone's project list through the existing app:get-projects read.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as the React Native app: the native Android client talks to one backend, has no SSH machines to pick from, and holds only the chat scope, which the project-clone: prefix refuses. Cloned projects reach it through the existing project list read with no client change.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change. The clone adds one row to the target's existing projects table through addProject and removes it again if the clone fails or is cut off by a restart. Clone progress is held in memory; a clone in progress is also listed in a new JSON file, project-clones.json in the backend's data folder, which is read once at start and emptied as each clone ends. A missing or unreadable file reads as empty, so an older backend that never wrote it and a newer one that finds a stale one both start cleanly; nothing in the SQLite database changes.

updateRelease.reason: Backend capabilities project_clone_v1 and, new, project_clone_folder_v1. The desktop checks project_clone_v1 before starting and shows 'too old to clone a project' without it. A folder other than the default is sent as the optional request field path, which an older target would drop and clone into ~/projects/<name> instead, so the desktop also needs project_clone_folder_v1 for a changed folder and otherwise shows 'too old to clone into another folder'; the default folder still works against a project_clone_v1 target because path is left out. An old desktop never sends path. No package identity, signing, deep link or update channel change.

automated: tests/unit/project-clone-integration.test.ts runs real git against local bare repositories: a branch tracking a fork clones the fork and checks out that branch; a never-pushed branch falls back to the default branch; no remote answers no-remote; a failed clone removes the folder and the project row; unsafe URLs, folder names and branch names are refused; only an ignored, text, under-cap, non-link file is offered and read; the target writes it with mode 0600, never over an existing file and never a tracked path; a forgotten favicon cache entry lets a new icon through; a chosen absolute or ~/ folder and an existing empty folder are cloned into, a non-empty one is refused and left alone, an existing folder is emptied but kept when the clone fails, and a second clone into a running folder is refused; a journal entry left by a cut-off clone removes the folder and project row it made and reads as failed, only empties a folder that existed before, never touches a folder or link that took its place, refuses a non-absolute or root path, and a corrupt journal reads as empty.

tests/unit/project-clone.test.ts pins the remote choice, the ignore-list filter, the text check, URL and folder-name checks, the progress line parser, and that a chat-scoped device cannot call project-clone channels, and the target folder check (absolute or ~/, no control characters, no . or .. part, no part starting with -).

tests/unit/project-clone-service.test.ts pins the desktop flow with a fake backend: it polls status, copies picked files source to target, reports files that failed, bumps the ready version that clears cached misses, resolves the send wait, and refuses a target without the capability, sends a chosen folder as path and leaves it out for the default, and refuses a chosen folder on a target without project_clone_folder_v1.
notExercised: Not run against a real SSH machine or the packaged app. The dialog, the inline sidebar progress and the send wait were checked by typecheck and the service test only, not watched in the running app.

A clone that needs credentials the target does not have (an SSH host alias from the desktop's ssh config, or a private HTTPS remote) fails with git's message; that path is covered only by the failed-clone test.

A real backend restart during a clone was not run: recovery is tested by writing the journal entry and the half-done folder that a killed backend leaves, then running the start-up recovery. A git child that outlives a killed backend is not stopped; recovery removes the folder under it and that git then fails.

The folder field, its inline check and Try again in the dialog were checked by typecheck only, not watched in the running app. Windows paths such as C:\\code on a Windows target are refused; only absolute POSIX and ~/ paths are accepted.
